claims.text: Mechanical alloying followed by spark plasma sintering can produce a dense bulk Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni-Ti multi-principal-element alloy.
High-energy ball milling produces an Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni-Ti nanocrystalline solid solution with grain size below 50 nm and mixed FCC and BCC phases.
SPS at 1200–1300 °C causes the Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni-Ti alloy to decompose into ordered B2 and disordered BCC phases.
A short SPS dwell at 1200–1300 °C avoids excessive grain or microstructural coarsening.
High configurational entropy together with the mixing enthalpy of the constituent elements drives B2+BCC decomposition.
The ordered B2 phase is Al-Ni rich, while the disordered BCC phase is Cr-Fe-Co rich, and the two phases form coherent interfaces.
The multi-principal-element structure creates severe lattice distortion.
Fine B2+BCC decomposition and lattice distortion impede dislocation motion and increase hardness.
Precipitation and lattice-distortion strengthening increase the alloy's density.
Cr in the BCC matrix rapidly forms a compact, self-healing Cr2O3 scale during high-temperature exposure.
The Cr2O3 scale acts as a diffusion barrier against both high-temperature oxidation and aqueous corrosion.
The B2 phase provides thermal stability to the processed alloy.
The SPS-processed alloy will have Vickers hardness above 600 HV.
Al and Ti make the alloy lightweight while SPS gives it a high packing fraction or bulk density.
The alloy will resist oxidation in air up to 800 °C better than single-phase solid-solution HEAs.
The alloy will show superior corrosion resistance in H2SO4 compared with single-phase solid-solution HEAs.
The Cantor alloy has less optimized high-temperature oxidation resistance because Mn forms non-protective oxides and is depleted from the bulk.
Keeping SPS below 1350 °C prevents grain coarsening and preserves mechanical properties.
Exceeding 1350 °C causes protective oxide-forming elements to dissolve into the bulk.
Adding Ti may change the thermodynamic driving force for B2 ordering and the stability of chromia.

contradictions.description: The target is described as both lightweight and as maximizing or achieving high density. High relative density or packing fraction could coexist with low intrinsic density, but the hypothesis does not distinguish these quantities.
The proposed Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni-Ti alloy is a six-component system, whereas the uncertainty field calls the specific system quinary/quaternary.

The target alloy contains no Mn, yet MnO is presented as a possible dominant oxide on the target sample. MnO is relevant to the Mn-containing Cantor control but not to the stated Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni-Ti composition.
